headline: Dolphins 28, Jets 25

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Miami scored touchdowns on its first two drives and took its first lead of the season on Malik Willis’ 7-yard pass to rookie Caleb Douglas. Willis scrambled in from 2 yards with 6 seconds left in the half to cap a 91-yard drive for a 21–7 lead. The Jets reached the Miami 1 in the fourth quarter but settled for a field goal, and Willis answered with a short toss that Douglas took 63 yards for a 28–17 lead with 4:55 left.

body.label: The finish
body.text: Geno Smith hit Mason Taylor for a touchdown and a two-point conversion to cut it to 28–25 with 3:24 left. Facing fourth-and-1 at the Jets 49 near the two-minute mark, Jeff Hafley kept the offense on the field and Willis pushed forward for 2 yards to seal it.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Willis went 14 of 21 for 208 yards and two touchdowns with 37 rushing yards and a score. Ollie Gordon II ran 25 times for 103 yards and a touchdown. Douglas, back from a three-game ankle absence, scored his first two NFL touchdowns. Greg Dulcich led the team with five catches for 86 yards.

body.label: Injuries
body.text: Safety Dante Trader Jr. hurt his left shoulder in the third quarter. Cornerback Julius Brents left with a stinger in the second half and returned in the fourth.

body.label: Takeaway
body.text: Zero turnovers and Miami’s highest point total of the season delivered Hafley’s first NFL win and avoided the franchise’s first 0–6 start since 2019. The offense completed only three passes after halftime, so the second-half stall is the next thing to fix.

next: New England Patriots at Miami on Sunday, November 1, at 4:25 p.m. ET.

hurricanes.headline: No. 1 Miami 52, Pittsburgh 23

body.label: Last week
body.text: Miami survived Florida State 43–35 in double overtime on October 17. Malachi Toney caught the go-ahead touchdown and threw the two-point conversion, and Bryce Fitzgerald’s interception ended it. Miami rose to No. 1 in the AP poll for the first time in 24 years.

body.label: Turning points
body.text: Pittsburgh punted on each of its first four drives without a first down as Miami built a 17–0 lead. The Canes scored twice in the final two minutes of the half, with a fumble recovery in between, to lead 31–7. Miami recovered an onside kick to open the third quarter and scored again.

body.label: Standouts
body.text: Darian Mensah and Toney carried the offense again, with Toney scoring on 19- and 53-yard catches. Mark Fletcher Jr.’s third-quarter touchdown run, the 33rd of his career, moved him into second on Miami’s all-time list. The defense held Pitt to 69 rushing yards.

body.label: Takeaway
body.text: Wearing 2001 throwbacks with that title team in the stands, Miami never trailed and stayed one of three unbeaten FBS teams. Pass coverage gave up five plays of 25-plus yards, including Blue Hicks’ 149 receiving yards.

hurricanes.next: At North Carolina on Saturday, October 31, at 7:30 p.m. ET.
